title: SDK mini-protocols: UX and structured fidelity notes
summary: Draft exploring a lightweight set of streaming mini-protocols to improve SDK ergonomics, enforce structured output progressively, and introduce safety/quality linting before tool calls.
body:
Context:
- Problem: teams build complex tool-call workflows on top of the Hosted API. Current streaming surface forces app authors to reimplement a lot of fallbacks/validation for partial/fragile outputs, and SDK ergonomics vary across languages. We need a small set of interoperable "mini-protocols" that sit between model output and app toolcalls to improve developer velocity and reduce runtime errors.

Goals (high level):
- Provide a compact, backwards-compatible set of conventions (mini-protocols) that SDKs can adopt to: enforce structured output progressively, run safety/quality lint checks before tool invocation, and give ergonomic primitives (typed callbacks, lazy tool proxies) for client apps.
- Make streaming the default path for interactive flows while keeping sync fallbacks trivial.
- Instrument telemetry so product can tune fidelity thresholds, lint rules, and fallback budgets per workload.

Non-goals:
- Not trying to define a full DSL for tool orchestration (that is a later step).
- Not replacing existing typed-output PRDs; this is an SDK-focused, pragmatic shim.

Mini-protocol concepts (names are placeholders):
1) progressive-schema (PS)
   - Idea: declare a target JSON schema (or lightweight shape) up-front; model may emit partial fragments. Each fragment is validated as it arrives. SDK exposes event hooks: onFragment(schemaPath, validatedFragment, confidence) and onComplete(validatedPayload).
   - Benefits: early validation, well-typed client handlers, ability to pre-resolve which tool will be needed before the full response.

2) safety-lint layer (SL)
   - Idea: a small rules engine (server-side + SDK shim) that runs against partial fragments and flags severity levels: info/warn/block. Lint rules include: PII leak heuristics, external-call-safety (e.g., does the fragment request an unscoped shell command?), and hallucination heuristics for high-cost tool calls.
   - Behavior: when SL returns block for a fragment that would trigger a tool call, the SDK provides structured reasons and a remediation flow: ask model to replan, auto-fallback to lower-impact tool, or surface to operator.

3) lazy-tool-proxy (LTP)
   - Idea: SDK exposes a lazy proxy for tool handles described in the schema. The proxy resolves to a real tool RPC only when the model output reaches the threshold (confidence + lint pass). Proxies are lightweight serializable references so they survive session resume.
   - Ergonomics: TypeScript example:
     // ps declares a tool field: { "tool": {"name":"calendar.create","args":{...}} }
     const toolRef = await session.get('tool'); // returns LazyToolProxy
     // safe invocation. proxy resolves only after SL passes or after explicit approve()
     await toolRef.invoke({ start: '2025-06-20' });

4) fidelity-shim (FS)
   - Idea: given variable latency/cost budgets, FS negotiates fidelity tiers with the server (summary-only, structured-without-entities, full-entities). SDKs provide helpers to downgrade tool calls automatically (e.g., call a cached summarizer instead of opening a DB write).

Telemetry + Observability:
- Telemetry events to emit: fragment_received, schema_validation_result, lint_result, proxy_resolution_latency, tool_invoke_decision (auto/denied/approved), fallback_taken, session_resume_mismatch.
- Tagging: route/model, customer-tier, latency-budget, inferred-confidence.
- Purpose: inform Optimize recommendations (batching/caching/quantization suggestions) and alerting (e.g., increased block rates by lint rule).

SDK ergonomics guidelines (cross-language):
- Default: streaming-first API surface with small sync wrappers. SDKs should expose three primitives:
  1) onFragment(handler): receives typed fragments as they validate against PS.
  2) getToolRef(path): returns LazyToolProxy with .invoke() and .approve() hooks.
  3) lintListener(handler): receives structured lint events and can veto or escalate.
- Language ergonomics:
  - TypeScript: promise-based fragments + async iterators, strong types for schema paths, first-class union types for partial vs complete fragments.
  - Python: generator-based streaming, dataclass wrappers for fragments, simple sync helpers that call into async loop when needed.
- Backwards compatibility: if client doesn't opt-in to PS/SL/LTP, server falls back to existing streaming tokens. Opt-in gate: pass header X-RI-Mini-Protocols: 1.0 (or SDK-internal flag).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- PS: SDK can declare schema and receive fragment events; fragments validated and delivered to app handlers in both TS and Python SDKs.
- SL: At least 6 lint rules active (PII heuristic, external-call, url-extraction, suspicious-credentials, high-cost-tool, contradictory-facts). SDK exposes lintListener that can veto tool invoke.
- LTP: Lazy proxies serializable across session pause/resume; proxy resolves only after lint pass or explicit .approve().
- FS: Two fidelity tiers supported (summary, full-structured); automatic fallback when budget exhausted.
- Telemetry: events emitted and visible in Console per-route; dashboards for lint-block rates.

Open questions / risks:
- How to define a "confidence" signal from models that is stable across model versions? (Research/Applied-ML follow-up).
- Performance: per-fragment validation may add CPU overhead on the host. We need a perf budget (e.g., <= 4ms per fragment at 95th pct). Prod infra team to advise.
- Security: lint rules with regexes might leak PII detection patterns; ensure logs redact sensitive matches.
- UX: If the model keeps emitting fragments that keep failing SL, we need an automatic escalation UX (retry with system prompt + operator review).

Implementation plan (phases):
Phase 0 (experiment): prototype PS + onFragment hook in TS SDK, server-side fragment validator as an optional pipeline stage. Run with 3 internal teams for 2 weeks.
Phase 1 (MVP): add SL engine server-side + SDK lintListener, implement LTP in TS and Python, add basic telemetry. Beta with selected customers.
Phase 2: integrate FS with Optimize so fidelity suggestions can be surfaced automatically; expand lint rule set and add UI in Console for per-rule tuning and rate limiting.

Dev tasks (rough):
- server: fragment validation service, lint engine, proxy token format (serializable JSON), telemetry schemas.
- sdk-ts: onFragment API, LazyToolProxy impl, lintListener, examples.
- sdk-py: generator-based streaming impl, LazyToolProxy shim, tests.
- console: telemetry dashboard, per-route lint rule toggles, visualization of fragment timelines.

Playbook: runtime behavior for blocked fragments
- SL BLOCK on pre-tool fragment -> SDK emits blocking event -> default action: hold tool proxy resolution and request model to replan with a safety system prompt (auto) -> if failure after N retries surface to operator via Console with session snapshot.

Example (sketch of message flow):
Client -> start streaming with header X-RI-Mini-Protocols:1.0 + schema {"task":"book-flight","tool":{"name":"airbook.create","args":{...}}}
Server streams: fragment #1: {"itinerary": {"legs": [ {"from":"SFO"} ]}, "tool": null } -> onFragment called, passes schema validation, SL returns INFO -> no proxy resolution.
Fragment #2: {"tool": {"name":"airbook.create","args":{"card": "<redacted>"}}} -> fragment validation fails SL (suspicious-credentials) -> SDK vetoes toolRef.invoke and issues replan request to model.

Notes to reviewers:
- Prioritize few high-value lint rules first (PII, external-shell, high-cost).
- We should align with Serving Runtime on per-fragment CPU budget; possible optimization: shard validation to a separate validation pool.
- Need legal input on what telemetry of suspicious content we can store.

Next steps (this sprint):
- Build prototype PS in TS SDK (owner: Liam) - 6d
- Draft server-side lint rule set + small rule runner (owner: Marisol) - 5d
- Define telemetry events and dashboard mockups (owner: Ethan) - 3d
- Sync with infra and applied-ml to validate perf and confidence signals (owners: infra, applied-ml)

TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm header semantics with API layer team
- [ ] Write initial lint rules and test corpus (PII examples)
- [ ] Build end-to-end demo for internal demo day

End of notes.
